text:
elaine: starting thread for the usage & billing console layout — uploaded a new Figma with three micro-variations: https://www.figma.com/file/def456/usage-billing-v3

elaine: main goals: make it immediately clear where spend is coming from (org vs project), let users see token-type breakdowns without extra clicks, and make invoices discoverable + exportable. Key ideas in Figma:
- Grid view: 3 cards (Spend overview, Usage breakdown, Recent invoices) stacked on desktop, single column on mobile
- Split view: left full spend chart, right collapsible panels for token breakdown and invoices
- Compact list: condensed rows for customers with many projects (focus on density)

maria: i prefer Split view for enterprise customers who want a persistent chart + drill panel. Grid is nicer for new users.

vikram: accessibility nits: animated transitions on the stacked chart cause motion issues for screen reader users and those with vestibular disorders. add reduced-motion preference and pause on hover. Also ensure chart tooltips are keyboard-focusable.

jess: microcopy: "Invoices" heading should show invoice count and last paid date: e.g., "Invoices (12) — last paid Mar 1, 2025". also prefer "Estimated total" vs "Total" when billing period isn't closed.

sam: question about token breakdown: do we show raw token counts, cost-per-token, or both? Users often want to see cost drivers: model name, tokens, and effective per-token rate.

elaine: propose showing three columns: tokens, model, and effective rate. hide model column behind a small chevron on narrow screens.

vikram: color palette: per-project colors need accessible contrast against grid background. propose 6 accessible swatches and a fallback pattern for print/export.

maria: org vs project toggle placement debate: header-level toggle (global context) vs inline dropdown in spend card. I vote header so it sticks as you navigate.

elaine: header-toggle wins for persistence. we'll show context pill: "Org: acme-inc > Project: marketing". users can pin project default in settings.

jess: invoices export: customers requested per-line timestamps and usage categories. suggested CSV columns:
```
invoice_id, invoice_date, billed_for_period_start, billed_for_period_end, project, usage_category, tokens, unit_rate, line_total
```
Also add an "Export visible" option that downloads CSV for current filters.

sam: charts: stacked bars vs stacked area for trends? stacked bars are easier to read for comparing daily contributions; area is nicer for long-term trend reading. maybe toggle between aggregated and detailed modes.

elaine: good point. add a small toggle: "Aggregation: daily / hourly / cumulative" next to chart. default daily for last 90 days.

vikram: keyboard nav checklist for the panels: focus order -> header toggle -> chart -> chart legend items -> breakdown list -> invoices list -> export button. ARIA labels for each control.

maria: UX for small orgs (1 project): hide org/project toggle and show single project name to reduce clutter.

billing-bot: invoice 2025-03-20 available for org:acme-inc, amount:$3,210.00 — /billing/invoices

elaine: action items:
- elaine: update Figma with Split view as baseline, add reduced-motion option and credits badge (ETA: Mon)
- sam: prototype CSV export including "Export visible" filters (ETA: Thu)
- vikram: produce accessible swatch set + ARIA checklist (ETA: Wed)
- jess: draft invoice microcopy and tooltip text for "Estimated total" vs "Billed total" (ETA: Mon)
- maria: validate header-toggle behaviour with analytics team (what should default be) (ETA: Fri)

maria: okay to lock Split view as baseline for next design review? i'm 👍

elaine: locking Split view for next review. thanks team! :rocket:
